title.narrative: Stöd till WFP/UNHAS i Burkina Faso 2023

description.narrative:
Insatsen syftar till att tillhandahålla säker, pålitlig och effektiv flygtjänst till humanitära- och utvecklingspartner i Burkina Faso. FN:s humanitära flygtjänst är tillgänglig för humanitära så väl som utvecklingsaktörer, därigenom möjliggörs tillträde i svåråtkomliga kontexter för genomförande, uppföljning och frakt av livsviktiga insatsvaror. Detta för att stödja ett effektivt humanitärt stöd och utvecklingsbistånd, samt möjliggöra framkomlighet till befolkningar i svåråtkomliga områden.
Syftet är att individer i behov ska kunna få få snabb och effektivt stöd, genom de tjänster och transport som tillhandahålls för humanitära partners och utvecklingsaktörer.

The contribution aim to provide safe, reliable and efficient air service to the humanitarian and development community in Burkina Faso. The UN's humanitarian air service is available to humanitarian as well as development actors, thereby enabling access in hard-to-reach contexts for implementation, follow-up and shipping of vital supplies. This in order to support effective and efficient humanitarian and development assistance and enable access to populations in to hard to reach areas.
The aim is that crises-affected communities will benefit from services and transportation provided to humanitarian and development partners, receiving timely and effective assistance.

The intervention will contribute to outcome objective of WFP's Strategic Outcome 6, of WFP Country Strategy Plan in Burkina 2018-2023: Humanitarian and Development partners benefit from common services that enable them to reach and operate in targeted areas all year.
The intervention will particularly support activity 9: Provide logistics support to partners as needed.
The specific objective of the intervention is therefore to: Provide safe, reliable and efficient air service (cargo and passenger support) to the humanitarian and development community in Burkina Faso, including NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations and diplomatic missions. This in order to support effective and efficient humanitarian and development assistance and enable access to populations in to hard to reach areas.

The United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) has been providing safe, reliable, costeffective and rapid air transport of passengers and cargo to the humanitarian and development community. This has enabled them to access and operate even in the most inaccessible areas of Burkina Faso in the context of the country's severely hampered road access. Thanks to contributions from donors including Sweden, and income generated by its partial cost recovery system, UNHAS has been able to maintain and expand its operations. In response to the growing demand for flights, UNHAS increased its fleet from two to three helicopters. The fleet comprised two Mi17s and a Super Puma. The percentage of cargo capacity offered against total capacity requested 94% with a planned of 100. UNHAS has demonstrated its ability to adapt to changing needs. To meet user organizations' demand for air services and to reach new destinations, flight schedules have been regularly revised. In concrete terms, in 2023 UNHAS carried 27,501 passengers (against a planned figure of 1600) and 1,231 tonnes (against a planned figure of 700) of essential light cargo to 20 scheduled and 12 ad hoc destinations throughout the country, with five newly introduced destinations. The most frequented destinations were Dori, Djibo, GoromGorom and Fada, accounting for 54 percent of all passenger traffic. UNHAS flight hours averaged 253 per month, an 80% increase on 2022. The UNHAS user community grew from 100 organizations in 2022 to 159 in 2023, of which 55 percent were international NGOs, 21 percent national NGOs, 23 percent UN agencies and 1 percent diplomatic missions and donors. UNHAS also continued to facilitate medical evacuations and security transfers of humanitarian personnel in times of need, with 39 security transfers and three body evacuations carried out during the year. Number of timely medical and security evacuations performed was 42. In 2023, WFP successfully established robust partnerships with local institutions and organizations, demonstrating a commitment to building strong partnerships with national responders to achieve objectives outlined in the Country Strategic Plan. Local partners were crucial in managing complex field operations, especially in challenging security conditions. WFPs engagement with local actors not only facilitates better access to these volatile environments but also ensures the seamless continuity of activities in the field.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
